'''Adreian DeAngleo Payne''' (February 19, 1991 – May 9, 2022) was an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and [[Orlando Magic]] as well as for several European and Asian teams. Payne played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]].

==High school career==
Payne played high school basketball for [[Jefferson Township High School (Dayton, Ohio)|Jefferson High School]]. He posted averages of 15.6 points, 11.3 rebounds and 4.0 blocks as a senior. As a senior, he led Jefferson to a Division IV state championship and a 19–5 record. The ''[[Dayton Daily News]]'' named him first-team All-Area.<ref name=Msu /> He was named a fourth-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Noah A. McGee |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/adreian-payne-former-michigan-state-185549527.html |title=Adreian Payne, Former Michigan State Basketball Star and NBA Player, Fatally Shot at 31 |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |date= |accessdate=May 11, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:US_Navy_111110-N-DR144-711_Michigan_State_University_basketball_player_Adreian_Payne_dunks_during_a_practice_in_the_basketball_arena_on_the_flight.jpg|thumb|left|Adreian Payne practicing before the 2011 [[Carrier Classic]]]]
As a freshman at [[Michigan State University]], Payne averaged 2.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, playing in 34 games.<ref name=Msu>{{cite web |title=5 Adreian Payne |url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/adreian_payne_725881.html |work=[[Michigan State Spartans]] |publisher=[[Michigan State University]] |access-date=February 27, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806202329/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/adreian_payne_725881.html |archive-date=August 6, 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> During that year he was diagnosed with permanent reduced lung capacity, an ailment which affected his stamina.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2012/01/michigan_states_adreian_payne_1.html |title=Michigan State's Adreian Payne on his lung condition_ 'I'm gasping for air and I can't get it' |work=mlive.com |date=January 20, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2018 |archive-date=February 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206131556/http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2012/01/michigan_states_adreian_payne_1.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/adreian-payne |title=Adreian Payne _ NBADraft.net |work=nbadraft.net |date=April 9, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2018 |archive-date=February 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206073554/http://www.nbadraft.net/players/adreian-payne |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Situational-Statistics-the-2014-Power-Forward-Crop-4627/ |title=DraftExpress – Situational Statistics_ the 2014 Power Forward Crop |work=draftexpress.com |date=June 21, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2018 |archive-date=February 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206002557/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Situational-Statistics-the-2014-Power-Forward-Crop-4627/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he led the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Spartans]]  in blocks (39) and finished seventh in the Big 10. In 37 games (36 starts), he averaged 7.0 points and 4.2 rebounds per game. He was an Academic All-Big Ten selection.<ref name=Msu />

As a junior, Payne led the Big Ten in free-throw percentage (.848) and blocked a total of 46 shots, good for sixth all-time for a Michigan State player. In 36 games (24 starts), he averaged 10.5 points and 7.6 rebounds in 25.6 minutes per game.<ref name=Msu /> Payne was named to the Second Team All Big Ten, along with Michigan State teammates [[Keith Appling]] and [[Gary Harris]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/2013AllBigTen.pdf |title=2012–13 All-Big Ten Men's Basketball Team |access-date=February 27, 2014 |date=March 11, 2013 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |work=BigTen.org |archive-date=March 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190325194928/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/2013AllBigTen.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== NCAA Tournament===

The Michigan State big man scored 41 points in a 93–78 win over Delaware, setting the pace for the 2014 NCAA Tournament. Moreover, Payne shot 17 of 17 from the free-throw line, which set an NCAA Tournament record for most free throws made in a game without a miss.

===Friendship with Lacey Holsworth===

started when Payne met Holsworth during a team-sponsored hospital visit in 2011 and the two began to text and talk frequently afterward.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adreian Payne Forms a Special Bond with center court on Senior Night and helped him cut down the nets after [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team]] won the [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Biggest Star of March Madness Is an 8-Year-Old Girl Fighting Cancer |url=http://mashable.com/2014/03/27/march-madness-lacey-michigan-state/ |publisher=Mashable.com |access-date=April 9, 2014 ==Professional career==

===Atlanta Hawks (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, Payne was selected with the 15th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-select-adreian-payne-15th-pick |title=Hawks Select Adreian Payne With 15th Pick |work=NBA.com |date=June 26, 2014 |access-date=June 26, 2014 |archive-date=June 30, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140630012039/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-select-adreian-payne-15th-pick |url-status=live }}</ref> On July 25, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Hawks after averaging 12.5 points and 7.0 rebounds during the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-first-round-draft-pick-adreian-payne |title=Hawks Sign First-Round Draft Pick Adreian Payne |work=NBA.com |date=July 25, 2014 |access-date=July 25, 2014 |archive-date=August 9, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140809080832/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-first-round-draft-pick-adreian-payne |url-status=live }}</ref> After managing five preseason games for the Hawks, he was ruled out for the start of the regular season with [[plantar fasciitis]] in his left foot.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.peachtreehoops.com/2014/10/31/7140263/adreian-payne-injury-hawks-rookie-out-with-plantar-fasciitis-in-his |title=Adreian Payne injury: Hawks' rookie out with plantar fasciitis in left foot |work=PeachTree Hoops.com |date=October 31, 2014 |access-date=October 31, 2014 |archive-date=November 3, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141103005814/http://www.peachtreehoops.com/2014/10/31/7140263/adreian-payne-injury-hawks-rookie-out-with-plantar-fasciitis-in-his |url-status=live }}</ref> He subsequently missed the first ten games of the season with the injury, and upon his return, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on November 20.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-assign-payne-fort-wayne-mad-ants |title=Atlanta Hawks Assign Payne To Fort Wayne Mad Ants |work=NBA.com |date=November 20, 2014 |access-date=November 20, 2014 |archive-date=December 3, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141203184141/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-assign-payne-fort-wayne-mad-ants |url-status=live }}</ref> He was recalled by the Hawks on November 23,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-recall-payne-fort-wayne-mad-ants |title=Atlanta Hawks Recall Payne From Fort Wayne Mad Ants |work=NBA.com |date=November 23, 2014 |access-date=November 23, 2014 |archive-date=December 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225070032/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-recall-payne-fort-wayne-mad-ants |url-status=live }}</ref> reassigned on November 28,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4899311 |title=Hawks Assign Payne, Jenkins to Mad Ants |work=OurSportsCentral.com |date=November 28, 2014 |access-date=November 28, 2014 |archive-date=December 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141206033538/http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4899311 |url-status=live }}</ref> and recalled again on |access-date=December 6, 2014 |archive-date=January 27, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150127024624/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/12/06/hawks-recall-adreian-payne.ap/index.html He recorded 2 points and 3 rebounds in 13 minutes of action as the Hawks lost 107–77.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141226/MILATL/gameinfo.html |title=Perfect 10: Dudley doesn't miss, Bucks rout Hawks |work=NBA.com |date=December 27, 2014 |access-date=December 27, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228180441/http://www.nba.com/games/20141226/MILATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 28, 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 30, the flexible assignment rule was again used to assign Payne to Austin.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-assign-john-jenkins-idaho-stampede-and-adreian-payne-austin-spurs |title=Atlanta Hawks Assign John Jenkins To Idaho Stampede and Adreian Payne To Austin Spurs |work=NBA.com |date=December 30, 2014 |access-date=December 30, 2014 |archive-date=January 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106155432/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-assign-john-jenkins-idaho-stampede-and-adreian-payne-austin-spurs |url-status=live }}</ref> He was recalled again on January 12, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4914762 |title=Atlanta Hawks Recall Adreian Payne from Austin Spurs |work=OurSportsCentral.com |date=January 12, 2015 |access-date=January 12, 2015 |archive-date=January 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150113053535/http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4914762 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2017)===
On February 10, 2015, Payne was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for a protected future first-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-acquire-forward-adreian-payne-atlanta |title=Wolves Acquire Forward Adreian Payne from Atlanta |work=NBA.com |date=February 10, 2015 |access-date=February 10, 2015 |archive-date=June 22, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622112822/https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-acquire-forward-adreian-payne-atlanta |url-status=live }}</ref> On March 9, 2015, while starting in place of [[Kevin Garnett]], he had a season-best game with 16 points, and 15 rebounds in an 89–76 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150309/MINLAC/gameinfo.html |title=Redick, Jordan lead short-handed Clippers past Wolves, 89–76 |work=NBA.com |date=March 9, 2015 |access-date=March 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151012103456/http://www.nba.com/games/20150309/MINLAC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 12, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On October 21, 2015, the Timberwolves exercised their third-year team option on Payne's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-exercise-team-options-five-players |title=Timberwolves Exercise Team Options on Five Players |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=October 21, 2015 |access-date=October 21, 2015 |archive-date=February 16, 2016 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20160216094321/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-exercise-team-options-five-players |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 25, 2016, using the flexible assignment rule, he was assigned to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]], the [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate of the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-assign-adreian-payne-erie-bayhawks-nba-development-league |title=Wolves Assign Adreian Payne to Erie BayHawks of NBA Development League |work=NBA.com |date=January 25, 2016 |access-date=January 25, 2016 |archive-date=January 26, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126171749/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-assign-adreian-payne-erie-bayhawks-nba-development-league |url-status=live }}</ref> He was recalled by the Timberwolves on February 1.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-recall-adreian-payne-nba-development-leagues-erie-bayhawks |title=Wolves Recall Adreian Payne from NBA Development League's Erie BayHawks |work=NBA.com |date=February 1, 2016 |access-date=February 1, 2016 |archive-date=February 2, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202094748/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-recall-adreian-payne-nba-development-leagues-erie-bayhawks |url-status=live }}</ref>

On February 7, 2017, Payne was ruled out indefinitely with a blood condition, having been treated for [[Thrombocytopenia|low platelet counts]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/adreian-payne-injury-update |title=ADREIAN PAYNE INJURY UPDATE |work=NBA.com |date=February 7, 2017 |access-date=February 8, 2017 |archive-date=February 11, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211105839/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/adreian-payne-injury-update |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2017/02/07/adreian-payne-out-indefinitely-with-blood-disorder/97623764/ |title=Adreian Payne out indefinitely with blood disorder |work=USAToday.com |date=February 7, 2017 |access-date=February 8, 2017 |archive-date=August 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814174923/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2017/02/07/adreian-payne-out-indefinitely-with-blood-disorder/97623764/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He returned to action in late March.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/paynead01/gamelog/2017/ |title=Adreian Payne 2016–17 Game Log |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=October 5, 2017 |archive-date=October 6, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006012353/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/paynead01/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2017–2018)===
On August 21, 2017, Payne signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Denton |first=John |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-adreian-payne-two-way-contract/ |title=Magic Sign Adreian Payne to Two-Way Contract |work=NBA.com |date=August 21, 2017 |access-date=October 5, 2017 |archive-date=October 10, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010075749/http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-adreian-payne-two-way-contract |url-status=live }}</ref> Under the stipulations of the deal, he spent the majority of the 2017–18 season with Orlando's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Lakeland Magic]]. On January 26, 2018, he was waived by Orlando after his name surfaced in an alleged sexual assault dating back to his freshman year in college. After an investigation, no charges were filed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-adreian-payne-waived-by-magic/ |title=Magic's Adreian Payne: Waived by Magic |work=cbssports.com |date=January 26, 2018 |access-date=January 26, 2018 |archive-date=January 27, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180127202341/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-adreian-payne-waived-by-magic/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Samman |first=Shaker |url=https://www.theringer.com/2018/1/26/16938074/michigan-state-sexual-assault |title=An 'Outside the Lines' Report Details Michigan State's Mishandling of Sexual Assault and Violence Accusations |work=theringer.com |date=January 26, 2018 |access-date=January 27, 2018 |archive-date=January 27, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180127002647/https://www.theringer.com/2018/1/26/16938074/michigan-state-sexual-assault |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Panathinaikos (2018)===
On February 5, 2018, Payne signed with the [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] for the remainder of the 2017–18 season. His best game was against Spanish club [[Valencia]] recording 12 points and grabbing 8 rebounds in 17 minutes. In the last game of the [[EuroLeague]] regular season, against [[Olimpia Milano]], he started for the first time. He finished the regular season averaging 3.5 points and 4 rebounds a game in a total of eight matches played.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=44881 |title=Payne in "green" |work=paobc.gr |date=February 5, 2018 |access-date=February 5, 2018 |language=el |archive-date=February 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206003350/http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=44881 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Nanjing Tongxi Monkey King (2018–2019)===
Payne started the season 2018–19 with the [[Nanjing Monkey Kings|Nanjing Tongxi Monkey King]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]], where he averaged 16.9 points and 8.6 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://basketball.asia-basket.com/China/news/552764/Adreian-Payne-(ex-Panathinaikos)-agreed-terms-with-Monkey-Kings |work=basketball.asia-basket.com |title=Adreian Payne (ex Panathinaikos) agreed terms with Monkey Kings |date=October 31, 2018 |language=en |access-date=January 15, 2019 |archive-date=January 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116050411/https://basketball.asia-basket.com/China/news/552764/Adreian-Payne-(ex-Panathinaikos)-agreed-terms-with-Monkey-Kings |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/562385/Panathinaikos-welcome-back-Payne,-ex-Nanjing-TX-MK |title=Panathinaikos welcome back Payne, ex Nanjing TX MK |work=eurobasket.com |language=en |access-date=January 15, 2019 |archive-date=January 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116050025/https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/562385/Panathinaikos-welcome-back-Payne,-ex-Nanjing-TX-MK |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Return to Panathinaikos (2019)===
On January 12, 2019, Payne and [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] reached an agreement that would bring the player back in Greece for a second stint with the EuroLeague club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/810093/panathinaikos-has-a-deal-with-adreian-payne/ |title=Panathinaikos has a deal with Adreian Payne |work=eurohoops.net |date=January 12, 2019 |language=en |access-date=January 15, 2019 |archive-date=January 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116050210/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/810093/panathinaikos-has-a-deal-with-adreian-payne/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 13, 2019, [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] signed the center to a deal for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9e7gu5oy86esfcfr/panathinaikos-payne-reunite |title=Panathinaikos, Payne reunite |work=euroleague.net |date=January 13, 2019 |language=en |access-date=January 15, 2019 |archive-date=January 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190115204702/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9e7gu5oy86esfcfr/panathinaikos-payne-reunite |url-status=live }}</ref>
On February 17, 2019, Payne helped [[Panathinaikos BC]] to win the [[Greek Basketball Cup]] title against [[PAOK BC]] ([https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/news/567535/Greek-Cup:-Panathinaikos-won-the-Greek-Cup-for-19th-time-after-beating-PAOK-79-73 79–73]). The final was held in [[Heraklion]], Sports Indoor Arena, [[Crete]]. Payne's second stint with the Greek club proved to be briefer than his first, as he was released on March 13, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/843367/adreian-payne-waived-by-panathinaikos-signing-with-asvel/ |title=Adreian Payne waived by Panathinaikos; signing with ASVEL |work=eurohoops.net |date=March 13, 2019 |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2019 |archive-date=November 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108001039/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/843367/adreian-payne-waived-by-panathinaikos-signing-with-asvel/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===ASVEL (2019–2020)===
On March 19, 2019, [[ASVEL Basket]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]] announced that they had signed Payne.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ldlcasvel.com/adreian-payne-renforce-ldlc-asvel/ |title=Adreian PAYNE renforce LDLC ASVEL |language=FR |date=March 19, 2019 |website=ldlcasvel.com |access-date=March 19, 2019 |archive-date=March 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321132709/https://ldlcasvel.com/adreian-payne-renforce-ldlc-asvel/ |url-status=live }}</ref> With ASVEL, Payne won the [[2018–19 Pro A season|2019 Pro A]] championship as well as the [[French Basketball Cup|French Cup]] that year.<ref>{{cite web|last=Benson |first=Pat |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/former-hawks-player-adreian-payne-dead-at-31 |title=Adreian Payne Passes Away at 31 Years Old - Sports Illustrated |publisher=Si.com |date= May 9, 2022|accessdate=May 11, 2022}}</ref>

===Ormanspor (2021)===
On February 25, 2021, Payne signed with [[OGM Ormanspor]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/adreian-payne-joins-ormanspor/ |title=Adreian Payne joins Ormanspor |last= |first= |date=February 25, 2021 |website= |newspaper=Sportando |language=En |access-date=February 26, 2021 |archive-date=March 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303111753/https://sportando.basketball/en/adreian-payne-joins-ormanspor/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Juventus (2021–2022) ===
In December 2021, Payne signed with the [[BC Juventus|Juventus Utena]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pakėnas |first1=Rokas |title=Utenos bomba: prisikvietė NBA ir Eurolygos arenose skraidžiusį puolėją |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/utena-paruose-bomba-laukiamas-nba-ir-eurolygos-arenose-skraides-puolejas-875-1613234 |website=[[15min.lt]] |access-date=December 18, 2021 |language=lt |archive-date=December 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214223821/https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/utena-paruose-bomba-laukiamas-nba-ir-eurolygos-arenose-skraides-puolejas-875-1613234 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Pakėnas |first1=Rokas |title=Žvaigždė Utenoje: kaip "Juventus" sužvejojo 15-ąjį NBA šaukimą? |url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/zvaigzde-utenoje-kaip-juventus-suzvejojo-15-aji-nba-saukima-875-1613824 |website=15min.lt |access-date=December 18, 2021 |language=lt |archive-date=December 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211218100838/https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/zvaigzde-utenoje-kaip-juventus-suzvejojo-15-aji-nba-saukima-875-1613824 |url-status=live }}</ref> He averaged 8.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game. Payne parted ways with the team on February 17, 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Juventus Utena, Adreian Payne part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/juventus-utena-adreian-payne-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=February 18, 2022 |date=February 17, 2022 |archive-date=February 17, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220217190606/https://sportando.basketball/en/juventus-utena-adreian-payne-part-ways/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Death==
On May 9, 2022, Payne was fatally shot in [[Orlando, Florida]], after he and his girlfriend had travelled to the home of Lawrence Dority in an attempt to prevent a [[Domestic violence|domestic dispute]].<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33892760/former-michigan-state-basketball-star-adreian-payne-fatally-shot-trying-prevent-domestic-dispute-police-investigation-reveals|title=Former Michigan State basketball star Adreian Payne fatally shot while trying to prevent domestic dispute, police investigation reveals|first=Myron|last=Medcalf|work=[[ESPN]]|date=May 10, 2022|accessdate=May 11, 2022}}</ref> Payne was transported to a hospital where he was pronounced dead. Dority claimed he felt threatened by Payne's 6'10" height and believed Payne was reaching for a weapon,<ref name="ESPN"/> but he was arrested and charged with first-degree murder after police determined that Payne had not posed a threat.<ref name="ESPN"/><ref>{{cite web |date=May 10, 2022 |title=Adreian Payne death: Doorbell video appears to capture audio of deadly shooting in Orlando |url=https://www.fox35orlando.com/news/adreian-payne-death-doorbell-video-appears-to-capture-deadly-shooting-in-orlando |url-status=live |access-date=May 10, 2022 |website=Fox 35 Orlando |archive-date=May 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511004657/https://www.fox35orlando.com/news/adreian-payne-death-doorbell-video-appears-to-capture-deadly-shooting-in-orlando}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Solari |first1=Chris |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2022/05/09/adreian-payne-dies-obituary/9702652002/ |title=Adreian Payne, former Michigan State basketball star, shot and killed Monday at age 31 |access-date=May 10, 2022 |work=Detroit Free Press |date=May 9, 2022 |archive-date=May 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220509200812/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2022/05/09/adreian-payne-dies-obituary/9702652002/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Dority was convicted of second-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petro |first=Allison |date=2025-08-29 |title=Man sentenced to life in prison for murder of former Orlando Magic player |url=https://www.wesh.com/article/lawrence-dority-sentenced-murder-of-former-orlando-magic-player/65933259 |access-date=2026-05-26 |website=WESH |language=en}}</ref>
